Well, I can't really help much because Windows 10 is a PITA. I recommend sticking with Windows 7, frankly, if you HAVE to dual boot. It sounds like you've got EFI problems. You will need to probably:

A) Backup all your data B) Go into the BIOS and figure out how to setup "legacy" boot option (no secure boot, no EFI, etc..)* C) Locate a clean copy of Win 7 x64 Pro D) Totally wipe the drive. I mean bare metal. E) Install a fresh copy of Win 7 x64 Pro F) Install LMDE2 x64 G) Retrieve your data.

I generally like to have a partition for data that is bigger than either OS partition and is shared between them as a large NTFS. That's a good place to put that data you backed up in step 1.

It's a pain in the ass to go through all that, but you'll have the best system in the long term, until you're ready to just dump Windows altogether, which is where I've been at for a couple of years now. :D

LMDE2 is the best OS in history though (in my opinion, and I've used a lot of OSes!), so good choice even being here!

The problem is that, starting with Windows 8, they introduced a whole new boot system called EFI or UEFI that replaces the BIOS boot of Windows 7 and before. Simply restoring or recreating the MBR in sector 0 and setting a primary partition to 'active' doesn't work anymore, unfortunately.

In EFI, the boot sector starts in sector 1, and simply points to a separate EFI partition where all of the grubbing and syslinuxing is handled. Your Grub menu is built up here, through scripts and directory trees. The menu entries then point to the corresponding bootable partitions

Ah, the good old days, where you could type out the 440 bytes of your bootsector in a hex editor to rescue a disc, and multibooting was just a matter of setting the right partition active...
